INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR AGREEMENT

This Independent Contractor Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of April 14, 2026 between Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 1400 Foundry Road, Akron, Ohio 44305 (the "Company"), and Rosalind Achebe Kwan, an individual residing at 14 Beech Row, Columbus, Ohio 43201 (the "Contractor").

1. SERVICES. The Contractor will provide the services described in Exhibit A (the "Services"). The Contractor controls the manner and means of performing the Services, sets her own hours, and may perform them at any location she chooses. The Company may specify the result required but not the method by which it is achieved.

2. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR STATUS. The Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee, partner, agent, or joint venturer of the Company. The Contractor is not eligible for any employee benefit, including health insurance, paid leave, retirement, or workers' compensation, and waives any claim to them. The Contractor is responsible for her own federal, state, and local taxes, including self-employment tax, and the Company will issue an IRS Form 1099-NEC. Neither party may bind the other.

3. NO EXCLUSIVITY. The Contractor may perform services for others, including competitors of the Company, provided she complies with Section 6. The Contractor holds herself out as available to the public and maintains her own business identity.

4. CONTRACTOR'S OWN RESOURCES. The Contractor supplies her own equipment, software, and workspace, and bears her own business expenses, except that the Company will reimburse pre-approved travel at cost. The Contractor bears the opportunity for profit and the risk of loss on each engagement.

5. FEES. The Company will pay $185 per hour for Services performed, on invoices submitted monthly and payable within thirty (30) days. Payment is by the project deliverable listed in Exhibit A, not by time worked at the Company's direction.

6. CONFIDENTIALITY. The Contractor will not use or disclose the Company's Confidential Information except to perform the Services, for three (3) years after disclosure. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits the Contractor from reporting a possible violation of law to a government agency, or from making a disclosure protected by 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b).

7. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY. All deliverables the Contractor creates specifically for the Company under this Agreement are works made for hire under the Copyright Act to the extent they qualify, and to the extent they do not, the Contractor assigns them to the Company. The Contractor retains ownership of any pre-existing material and any general skill, know-how, or tool she uses, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the deliverables.

8. NO NON-COMPETE. Nothing in this Agreement restricts the Contractor from working for anyone after it ends. The Contractor's only continuing obligations are in Sections 6 and 7.

9. INSURANCE. The Contractor maintains commercial general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000, and will name the Company as an additional insured on the general liability policy.

10. INDEMNIFICATION. Each party will indemnify the other against third-party claims arising from its own negligence or wilful misconduct, and the Contractor will indemnify the Company against any claim that a deliverable infringes a third party's intellectual property.

11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. Except for the indemnities in Section 10 and a breach of Section 6, neither party is liable for indirect or consequential damages, and each party's aggregate liability is limited to the fees paid in the twelve months before the claim.

12. TERM AND TERMINATION. This Agreement runs for one year and does not renew automatically. Either party may terminate for convenience on fifteen (15) days' written notice, and for material breach not cured within ten (10) days of written notice. On termination the Company pays for Services performed through the termination date, and Sections 2, 6, 7, 10, 11, and 13 survive.

13. GOVERNING LAW. Ohio law governs. Venue lies in the state and federal courts in Franklin County, Ohio.

HALBROOK DIAGNOSTICS, INC.                CONTRACTOR
